entries.name: Hypnosis
entries.content: A hypnosis, or a trance is a state at which a subject is near sleeping with their entire attention being drawn to the voice of the person speaking. During hypnosis the subconscious mind takes over which makes hypnosis the perfect state to take in any suggestion. The deeper a target is into hypnosis, the more likely they are to accept a suggestion. The deeper a subject is into hypnosis the less they move on their own and the less they talk. When awakening from a trance, a subject may remember what happened during a trance if the trance was light however they may not remember what happened during the trance if the hypnosis was deep.

entries.name: Inductions
entries.content: Induction is a part of the hypnosis where the hypnotist guides the target to the state of hypnosis. Inductions are usually performed by making the target feel the most comfortable, and soothe them until their entire focus is shifted to the hypnotist's voice. A subject falls deeper into a trance the calmer and more relaxed they feel, and so, explaining how the target can feel how comfortable they are sitting on whatever they are sitting on, explaining how calmness is washing over them, explaining how their worries slowly fade away are he best, and making the subject focus on the hypnotist's voice ar ethe best strategies to hypnotize. However using a strategy like swinging a pendulum can also prove useful by making the target look at the pendulum and focus on only the motion and the hypnotist's voice until they let go of every other thought and fall deep under trance.

entries.name: Susceptibility
entries.content: susceptibility is how easily a subject falls under a trance, the more suggestible they are, the easier they fall under a trance. the less susceptible they are, the less likely they are to fall under a trance.

entries.name: Suggestions
entries.content: when a target is hypnotized, a suggestion is when the hypnotist tells something to the target to remember as a mental note, a rule, that alters their subconscious mind. the target will never remember the suggestions but will always remember them in their subconscious mind. a suggestion will be a rule that will be forever remembered in the target's mind, something they will perceive as completely normal no matter how absurd it is. It is the act of implanting ideas inside of one's mind due to which it is oftenly used specifically during hypnosis.

entries.name: Orders
entries.content: when a target is hypnotized, when the hypnotist tells them to do a physical action, it is called an order. the order can be any physical activity, including talking.

entries.name: Triggers
entries.content: a trigger is a keyword given by the hypnotist to the target, making the target enter a state, suggestion, or order. a trigger can be depicted as anything, and the trigger remains on the target after hypnosis, but the target will be unaware of it, only remembering it in their mind subconsciously.

entries.name: Fractionation
entries.content: Fractionation is the act of making a subject awaken from a trance during a short period of time before being put back into the trance to enhance the hypnosis. Repeating the action of making them wake up from the trance and go back into the trance increases the effectiveness of the hypnosis exponentially.

entries.name: Conditioning
entries.content: Conditioning is the act of making someone believe something. Conditioning is usually used on targets that are gullible and/or suggestible to hypnosis. Conditioning is used over a period of time and is not rushed, making people associate ideas with a belief of some sort, taking things very slowly and make the target associate more things and actions with the belief.

entries.name: Common Sense
entries.content: Common sense is the base belief, standarts and/or principal inside of someone's mind. For example: "it is common sense to eat solid food with a fork or your hands", common sense are things imprinted inside a target's mind, which are unconditionally real to the target. So, since it is logically common sense to feel bad from insults, altering their common sense and making the target like the insults instead will make them associate it as if it was always normal and natural.

entries.name: Mind
entries.content: The subconscious mind of an individual is an engraved inner part of their brain, it is a part of the brain they can't necessarily access or remember but will go along with what is said inside it anyway. Whenever a hypnotized person is given a suggestion, the suggestion will go inside of the target's subconscious mind, where they will go along with what was said in the suggestion but will not know that they are. Orders may also make the brain forget certain memories.

entries.name: Gaslighting
entries.content: One method of manipulation involves making someone doubt their own reality or perception, often by denying facts, lying, or contradicting their experiences.

entries.name: Guilt-tripping
entries.content: Manipulators use guilt to control others, often by making them feel responsible for the manipulator's emotions or problems.

entries.name: Love Bombing
entries.content: Love bombing can be used to manipulate someone by overwhelming them with affection and attention to gain control or influence over them. This is typically followed by periods of coldness or withdrawal to maintain desire.

entries.name: Negging
entries.content: Undermining someone's self-esteem, with backhanded compliments or subtle insults, makes them more vulnerable to manipulation.

entries.name: Isolation
entries.content: Cutting off someone's connections with others, making them more dependent on the manipulator for social interaction and support, is a common form of manipulation.

entries.name: Fearmongering
entries.content: Fear can be used to influence and manipulate someone's decisions, often by exaggerating risks or consequences.

entries.name: Playing the Victim
entries.content: Manipulators portray themselves as a victim of circumstances, or others' actions, to gain sympathy and avoid responsibility.

entries.name: Triangulation
entries.content: Triangulation involves bringing a third person into the dynamics of the relationship, often to create competition, insecurity, or to validate the manipulator’s perspective.

entries.name: Silent Treatment
entries.content: Withholding communication or affection to punish or control the other person is a common form of manipulation.

entries.name: False Promises
entries.content: Offering something desirable without any intention of following through can be used to manipulate, to maintain control, or keep someone engaged.

entries.name: Selective Memory
entries.content: Claiming to forget events or conversations, often to gaslight or avoid accountability, is a common method of manipulation.

entries.name: Excessive Compliments
entries.content: Flattery can be used to lower someone's guard or to distract them from the manipulator's less desirable actions.

entries.name: Coercion
entries.content:
Coercion is a powerful tool often employed by manipulators or abusers to gain control over others. It involves applying pressure, persuasion, or force to make someone perform an action against their will or beliefs. Common tactics used in coercive scenarios include threats, intimidation, isolation, and exploitation of vulnerabilities.

In a nonconsensual context, coercion can lead to individuals feeling trapped, fearful, or unable to resist unwanted advances. This dynamic may have lasting effects on the victim's sense of self, trust, and ability to form healthy relationships. 

Key Takeaways:

-Coercion is a method used to control or manipulate someone against their will.
-It can involve various tactics, such as threats, isolation, and exploitation of vulnerabilities.

entries.name: Intimidation
entries.content:
to frighten or threaten someone, usually in order to persuade them to do something that you want them to do

Intimidation techniques can be physical, verbal, or psychological. They can include threats, isolation, and spreading rumors. 

Physical intimidation Using body size to force someone into an uncomfortable space, Standing over someone, Slamming doors, Throwing things, and Punching or kicking walls or furniture. 

Verbal intimidation 
Yelling and screaming
Using sarcasm, rudeness, or condescension
Patronizing or degrading someone
Psychological intimidation 
Gaslighting, which involves making someone doubt their memory, sanity, or perception
Isolation, which involves separating someone from their support network
Spreading rumors to damage someone's reputation
Other intimidation tactics 
Establishing dominance
Making threats to retaliate legally, economically, or physically
Intimidation can cause fear of injury or harm, and apprehension.

entries.name: Manipulation
entries.content:
Manipulation tactics include emotional manipulation, gaslighting, love-bombing, and isolation. 
Emotional manipulation 
Guilt tripping: Making someone feel guilty to control them
Fear, shame, or anger: Using fear, shame, or anger to make someone act in a certain way
Threats: Using threats of harm, punishment, or humiliation to control someone
Criticism: Using criticism to control someone
Lying: Using lies to control someone
Gaslighting 
Distorting reality to make someone doubt themselves and their beliefs
Love-bombing 
Escalating affection too quickly to form trust with someone and control them
Isolation
Separating someone from their friends and family 
Convincing someone to identify more with the manipulator than with their peers or supervisors 
Other manipulation tactics: 
Withholding affection or attention
Intimidation
Verbal abuse
Blackmail
Insulting
Deceiving
Cyber abuse, such as posting personal information online or spreading rumors
Manipulation is a form of psychological abuse. It can be unfair, mean, and damaging.

Sexual assault can take many different forms and be defined in different ways, but one thing remains the same: it’s never the victim’s fault.

Child Sexual Abuse
When a perpetrator intentionally harms a minor physically, psychologically, sexually, or by acts of neglect, the crime is known as child abuse.

Sexual Assault of Men and Boys
Men and boys who have been sexually assaulted or abused may also face some additional challenges because of social attitudes and stereotypes about men and masculinity.

Intimate Partner Sexual Violence
A perpetrator can have any relationship to a victim, and that includes the role of an intimate partner.

Incest
Regardless of how the law defines incest, unwanted sexual contact from a family member can have a lasting effect on the survivor.

Drug-Facilitated Sexual Assault
In cases of drug-facilitated sexual assault, survivors often blame themselves. Remember—you are not to blame. You are the only one allowed to make choices for your body. Using drugs or alcohol is never an excuse for assault and does not mean that it was your fault.

entries.name: sexual torture
entries.content:
Torture that is sexual in nature, or greatly harms one sexually.

(a) A person commits the crime of sexual torture if he or she does any of the following:

(1) Penetrates the vagina, anus, or mouth of another person with an inanimate object, by forcible compulsion, with the intent to sexually torture, sexually abuse, or to gratify the sexual desire of either party.

(2) Penetrates the vagina, anus, or mouth of a person who is incapable of consent by reason of being incapacitated, with an inanimate object, with the intent to sexually torture, sexually abuse, or to gratify the sexual desire of either party.

(3) Penetrates the vagina, anus, or mouth of a person who is less than 12 years old, with an inanimate object, by a person who is 16 years old or older with the intent to sexually torture, sexually abuse, or to gratify the sexual desire of either party.

(4) By inflicting physical injury, including, but not limited to, burning, crushing, wounding, mutilating, or assaulting the sex organs or intimate parts of another person, with the intent to sexually torture, sexually abuse, or to gratify the sexual desire of either party.

entries.name: FORCIBLE COMPULSION
entries.content: Use or threatened use, whether express or implied, of physical force, violence, confinement, restraint, physical injury, or death to the threatened person or to another person. Factors to be considered in determining an implied threat include, but are not limited to, the respective ages and sizes of the victim and the accused; the respective mental and physical conditions of the victim and the accused; the atmosphere and physical setting in which the incident was alleged to have taken place; the extent to which the accused may have been in a position of authority, domination, or custodial control over the victim; or whether the victim was under duress. Forcible compulsion does not require proof of resistance by the victim.
